subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser private-network SSRF confirmation or allow/block policy, and which core policy shape is approved for metadata blocking, prompts, and config compatibility?
rationale: The request changes the browser egress security boundary and public config/CLI surface, and current source has no existing confirmation or temporary-grant contract that automation can safely extend without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve staged core policy
options.body: Start with a narrow explicit allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata behavior, then revisit interactive confirmation once the core contract is proven.

options.title: Approve interactive confirmation now
options.body: Define user approval UX, timeout, rate-limit, audit, redirect, and DNS rebinding semantics across browser navigation before implementation.

options.title: Keep current strict/opt-in model
options.body: Reject new core policy surface for now and document that private-network access remains an explicit trusted-environment opt-in with hostname exceptions.

recommendation.title: Approve staged core policy
recommendation.body: Start with a narrow explicit allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata behavior, then revisit interactive confirmation once the core contract is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged browser CDP/SSRF policy work and related test commits make this the best available routing signal for a security-boundary decision.
